newsitem.title: UK: Major says arguments "in both directions" over EMU.
newsitem.headline: Major says arguments "in both directions" over EMU.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday there were arguments "in both directions" over European economic and monetary union.
"If there were not arguments in both directions, we would not have kept our options (on EMU)," Major told parliament.

On Wednesday, Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said that on balance the government was "hostile" to European economic and monetary union (EMU). Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke later dismissed the comments as a "slip of the tongue".
Overnight, the two ministers issued a joint statement to Reuters saying there was no change to the government's wait-and-see policy over European economic and monetary union.
They said they were both hostile to EMU if it was undertaken on a non-convergent basis.
